newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's AWB sells 2,000 t. wheat in tender 27.
newsitem.headline: Australia's AWB sells 2,000 t. wheat in tender 27.

text.p: The Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Wednesday it sold 2,000 tonnes of new crop 1997/98 Australian Hard wheat at A$200 a tonne for Geelong delivery in its latest tender for domestic sales from its national pool.
Bids were received for 39,000 tonnes of current crop wheat and for 38,000 tonnes of 1997/98 wheat.
All 1996/97 season bids were rejected as they were below current domestic market prices, it said.
The reserve prices of this tender represent an increase from the previous tender two weeks ago which more accurately reflect the tightness in domestic supply in some regions, it said.

As this was a significant deviation from previous market signals provided through the tender system, a special tender will be held on Friday, July 11, to offer customers a further opportunity to secure supply, the AWB said.
The next tender would normally be held in two weeks time.
It said its reserve price for Australian Standard White (ASW) wheat was A$203.24 a tonne, Geelong delivery, for current crop wheat and A$183.24 for new season wheat.
The highest failed bids for Geelong ASW were A$192 a tonne for the current crop and A$180 for new crop wheat.
